## GET /admin-api/xacml

`getXacml`

**The Policy Decision Point settings and current status**

The Settings tab on /admin/xacml, as JSON.

THIS IS THE ONLY FAMILY ON THIS SERVICE THAT ANSWERS A QUESTION ABOUT SOMEBODY ELSE'S BOUNDARY. Every other protocol here authenticates or provisions a person; this one is handed a subject who was authenticated somewhere else and asked whether they may.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-condition

`addXacmlCondition`

**Add a Condition to a rule**

A boolean expression evaluated AFTER the Target matches. **At most one per rule** — the schema allows exactly one, and the editor stops offering this on a rule that has one rather than offering it and then refusing, because an option that is offered and refused teaches a caller that the menu is not to be trusted.

It must evaluate to EXACTLY ONE BOOLEAN. A condition returning a bag, or an integer, is a static type error and the policy is refused at write time rather than going Indeterminate on every request.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

`addXacmlMatch`

**Add a Match to an alternative**

One attribute tested against one value. It arrives COMPLETE AND VALID — a function, a literal and a designator — because an editor that produced half-built elements would hold a document that cannot be saved, and a document that cannot be saved cannot be evaluated, which is when you most want to look at it. ## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-policy

`addXacmlPolicyToSet`

**Add a Policy inside a PolicySet**

A PolicySet holds POLICIES; a Policy holds RULES. They are not two spellings of one thing, and asking for a rule on a policy set is refused rather than written somewhere it will not be read.

The new policy arrives with `deny-unless-permit` and no rules, which decides Deny. That is deliberate: this editor is LIVE, so a child added to the running root takes effect on the next request, and one that began permissive would be a hole opened by pressing Add.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-policy-reference

`addXacmlPolicyReference`

**Reference a policy stored separately in the repository**

THIS IS HOW A PDP REACHES MORE THAN ONE DOCUMENT. Evaluation starts at the root policy and a `PolicyIdReference` is resolved against the repository WHEN A DECISION IS MADE, not when the document is loaded — so referencing a policy that has not been written yet is allowed and is not an error. An unresolved reference is reported on the decision instead, which is what keeps the order two policies are authored in from mattering.

The `ref` is the PolicyId INSIDE the other document, not its directory entry name.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

| `policy` | string | yes | The directory entry name of the policy to edit — the `cn` under ou=policies, not the PolicyId inside the document. |
| `ref` | string |  | The PolicyId being referenced. Any URI. |
| `version` | string |  | An optional version constraint. Omit for no constraint. |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-rule-obligation

`addXacmlRuleObligation`

**Add an obligation to a rule**

Fires when this RULE's Effect is the decision. An obligation is the half of a decision that says "yes, AND you must also do this", and section 7.2 makes it binding: a PEP that cannot discharge one MUST NOT grant the access. ## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-target-anyof

`addXacmlTargetClause`

**Add a Target clause to a policy, a rule or a Target**

A `<Target>` is a list of clauses and **every one of them must match** — they are ANDed. Inside a clause the alternatives are ORed and inside an alternative the Matches are ANDed again, so the quantifier flips at each of the three levels.

That is why the element names read backwards from what they do: `AnyOf` holds `AllOf` holds `Match`, and the `AnyOf`s themselves are ANDed. Getting it wrong produces a policy that applies to more or less than was meant and never an error.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributeId` | string |  | The attribute to read. A bare name or the `urn:sts:xacml:attribute:` prefix reaches the directory through the PIP; anything else must be in the request. |
| `category` | string |  | The attribute category. Defaults to access-subject. |
| `matchId` | string |  | The match function. Defaults to string-equal. THE DATATYPE FOLLOWS IT on both sides, so choosing the function settles the literal's type and the designator's together. |
| `path` | string |  | The node's address, from GET /admin-api/xacml/editor. ONLY VALID AGAINST THE DOCUMENT IT WAS READ FROM: remove rule 0 and every path naming rule 1 now means rule 0. |
| `policy` | string | yes | The directory entry name of the policy to edit — the `cn` under ou=policies, not the PolicyId inside the document. |
| `value` | string |  | The literal to test against. |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/add-variable

`addXacmlVariable`

**Add a VariableDefinition to a policy**

Names an expression so several rules can share it — and so it is evaluated ONCE per request rather than once per use.

ITS SCOPE IS THE POLICY IT IS ON. A sibling policy in the same set cannot name it (section 5.24), which is why GET /admin-api/xacml/editor is the only reliable source of what a VariableReference at a given path may legally name.

It arrives holding a designator, because a VariableDefinition with no expression is a document that will not load. Replace it with any of the set-expression actions.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

| `policy` | string | yes | The directory entry name of the policy to edit — the `cn` under ou=policies, not the PolicyId inside the document. |
| `variableId` | string |  | The name. Defaults to the next free `v<n>`. A duplicate is refused — the reader rejects a document defining one id twice, so allowing it here would write a policy this service cannot load back. |

## GET /admin-api/xacml/authzen

`getXacmlAuthzen`

**The AuthZEN API: its settings, attribute catalogue and callers**

Everything the AuthZEN tab on /admin/xacml draws: whether /access/v1 answers in this realm, how its callers authenticate (authzen.callerAuthentication), the AuthZEN settings, the attribute catalogue on the sts-authzen-api object with the vocabulary a row may use, and the members of roles.authzenPepGroup with the applications each may ask about and the access request callback URLs registered for it, and the realm's AuthZEN access requests (#1180). `?caller=<name or DN>` looks one caller up, in the group or not.

Writes one authzenAttribute value on the realm's sts-authzen-api object, replacing the row for the same object and property. Refused for a row the catalogue's grammar refuses (STS-AUTHZEN-0010) and for one mapping onto a reserved identifier (STS-AUTHZEN-0011, 0012): a request-supplied attribute suppresses the PIP. ## POST /admin-api/xacml/create-from-template

`createXacmlPolicy`

**Create a policy from a template**

A template is a working, valid, evaluable policy in a shape people actually write — the first twenty clicks of the editor already made. `template` names one (see GET /admin-api/xacml/policies), `name` names the directory entry, and each parameter is sent as `p_<name>`; anything omitted takes the template's own default, so a call with only `template` produces the documented example.

`blank` is the one template that is not an example: it builds an EMPTY Policy, or an empty PolicySet with `p_kind=policyset` — which is the only way to create one of those without ALFA. An empty deny-unless-permit document DENIES rather than answering NotApplicable, so build it before making it the root.

A template BUILDS THE MODEL and the writer serializes it, rather than substituting into XML text — so a role called `a"b` cannot produce a document that will not parse.

The FIRST policy in an empty repository becomes the root, because a repository with a policy and no root decides nothing.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Names the DIRECTORY ENTRY. The PolicyId inside the document is a separate identifier and may be any URI. |
| `template` | string | yes | Which template. GET /admin-api/xacml/policies lists them with the parameters each takes. |

**200**: The operation was applied.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `problems` | list |  |  |
| `problems[]` | string |  |  |
| `what` | string |  |  |
| `why` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## GET /admin-api/xacml/decide

`getXacmlDecision`

**Ask the PDP about somebody and see the decision, which policies applied, and what the embedded PEP would do with it**

Everything the Try a decision tab on /admin/xacml draws. `subject`, `action` and `resource` are query parameters; with none of them it answers `asked: false` rather than deciding about nobody.

THE DECISION AND THE ENFORCEMENT ARE TWO DIFFERENT ANSWERS and both are here, which is the whole point of the page: the PDP says Permit, Deny, NotApplicable or Indeterminate, and the PEP then applies its bias and the obligation rule to get to allowed or refused. When a policy "is not working" it is nearly always because only one of those was being looked at.

This is NOT POST /xacml/pdp. That endpoint takes a JSON Profile request and is what a PEP calls; this builds a three-category request out of three parameters and is what a person asks.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The decision, what applied, and what the embedded PEP would do.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/delete

`deleteXacmlPolicy`

**Remove a policy from the repository**

Deleting the ROOT leaves the repository deciding nothing, and the reply says so rather than letting it be discovered by a Deny.

AN APPLICATION'S FINE-GRAINED POLICY (#564) is deleted only when no application names it in appFgaPolicy — an orphan of a deleted application (`applicationPolicies` on GET /admin-api/xacml/policies marks which). ## POST /admin-api/xacml/disable-pep

`disableXacmlPep`

**Stop nudging a registered remote PEP**

IT DOES NOT STOP IT ENFORCING, and the reply says so rather than letting that be discovered. A remote PEP holds its own copy of the engine and its own copy of the policy; nothing in this API reaches into another process. What changes is that this service no longer dials it when the repository changes, so it converges only on its own polling interval.

Named with a `-pep` suffix rather than reusing `disable` because this endpoint dispatches on the action name across the whole family, and a second `disable` would be ambiguous between a policy and a PEP.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

## GET /admin-api/xacml/editor

`getXacmlEditor`

**One policy as an editable tree, with what may legally be added at each node**

Everything the Policy editor tab on /admin/xacml draws. `?policy=<name>` chooses one; without it, the root.

Each node in `tree` carries `options.additions` — the elements XACML allows AT THAT POINT, computed against the real function library by the same code that validates the result. That is what makes this usable as an API and not only as a page: a caller can walk the tree, read the legal moves, and POST one, without a second copy of the grammar.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

## POST /admin-api/xacml/import-alfa

`importXacmlAlfa`

**Create a policy from ALFA**

ALFA — the Abbreviated Language For Authorization — is the readable syntax for XACML: forty lines of XML are eight of ALFA. Send it as `alfa` and a name as `name`.

IT IS PARSED, CONVERTED AND STORED AS XACML XML. The repository holds ONE representation, because two would be two documents that could disagree — GET /admin-api/xacml/editor renders the ALFA back from the model whenever you want to read it.

EVERY ATTRIBUTE MUST BE DECLARED BEFORE IT IS USED. That is ALFA's own rule and it is the most useful refusal in the parser: a typo in an attribute name is otherwise a policy that quietly matches nothing, which looks exactly like a policy that is working and denying you.

ALFA IS AN OASIS COMMITTEE SPECIFICATION DRAFT, not a ratified standard — no conformance suite, no schema, no second implementation to disagree with. The contract offered is the one that can be kept: anything this service EMITS as ALFA it reads back, and the policy decides identically either way.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alfa` | string | yes | The ALFA source. Parsed, converted and stored as XACML XML — the repository holds ONE representation. |
| `name` | string | yes | Names the directory entry. |

**200**: The operation was applied.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/issue-pep-certificate

`issueXacmlPepCertificate`

**Issue a remote PEP the certificate and private key for its HTTPS listener**

Generates a key pair and certifies it from the Remote PEP listeners (`pep-tls`) Issuing CA of THE REALM THE PEP REGISTERED TO — the realm this call is made in, because ou=peps is per realm — so a client that installed this service's Root CA verifies the PEP, and the chain says which realm vouched for it. A realm whose branch was built before that Issuing CA existed gets it added under its existing Intermediate; nothing already issued is replaced.

The PEP must be REGISTERED: its row is the one record that it exists in this realm. That is not a permission check on the PEP — registering is still not what lets it pull or enforce.

THE CERTIFICATE NAMES the PEP's registered name (where that is a DNS name) and the host of its notify URL, plus any `dnsNames` and `ipAddresses` sent. It certifies `serverAuth` and nothing else.

**THE PRIVATE KEY IS IN THIS REPLY AND NOWHERE ELSE.** This service records the certificate — its issuer's CRL and OCSP responder answer for it — and keeps no copy of the key, so nothing can read it back. To put the pair in the container, write `fullChainPem` (the leaf followed by its Issuing CA, the realm Intermediate and, since #1064, the service Root) and `privateKeyPem` to the files `PEP_HTTPS_CERT` and `PEP_HTTPS_KEY` name; the PEP picks up a pair written after it started. `anchorPem` is the service Root a client of that listener installs.

Issuing again REPLACES: the certificate it replaces goes on its issuer's revocation list as `superseded` (`replacedSerialHex`).

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer |  | The lifetime. Defaults to `pki.leafLifetimeDays`, and is shortened to the Issuing CA's own expiry. |
| `dnsNames` | list, or string |  |  |
| `dnsNames[]` | string |  |  |
| `ipAddresses` | list, or string |  |  |
| `ipAddresses[]` | string |  |  |
| `keyAlg` | one of `ec-p256`, `ec-p384`, `ec-p521`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `rsa-4096` |  | The key algorithm. Defaults to `ec-p256`. Only the RSA and NIST-curve ECDSA keys a TLS stack serves are offered. |
| `name` | string | yes | The registered PEP's name, as GET /admin-api/xacml/peps lists it. |

**200**: The operation was applied.

## GET /admin-api/xacml/monitor

`getXacmlMonitor`

**How many authorization decisions are being made, by which enforcement point, and how many are refusals**

Everything /admin/xacml/monitor draws: the global figures — policies, enforcement points, decisions, allows, declines — and then every PEP with its own counts, EMBEDDED and REMOTE in one list.

**A DECISION IS NOT AN ENFORCEMENT.** XACML has four decisions (Permit, Deny, NotApplicable, Indeterminate) and a PEP has two outcomes, and what maps between them is the PEP's BIAS: a deny-biased PEP refuses a NotApplicable that a permit-biased one allows, from the same decision on the same request. An obligation the PEP cannot discharge also turns a Permit into a refusal (section 7.2) — the one enforcement outcome that looks like a bug from the client side and is the specification working. So `allowed` is not `permit`, and both are reported.

**WHAT THIS SERVICE SAW IS NOT WHAT IT WAS TOLD.** `decisions.here` was counted by this process as it happened; `decisions.remote` is what registered PEPs REPORT on their heartbeats, cumulative in their own memory, and a PEP that restarts makes it go down. `decisions.combined` adds the two, which is the figure a deployment wants and is arithmetic over two kinds of evidence rather than a measurement.

**THE EMBEDDED PEPS ARE NOT "REGISTERED" AND CANNOT BE.** They are compiled into this process, so their existence is a fact about the build. A remote PEP registers because it has no other way to be known about — and even that is not a permission: an unregistered PEP can pull GET /xacml/pep/policies and enforce perfectly, and appears here nowhere. This is every enforcement point the service KNOWS ABOUT, which is a smaller claim than every one that exists.

The counters are IN MEMORY, start with the process (`since`) and are per trust realm. The durable record of a refusal is GET /admin-api/audit, which has the reason as well as the count.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml/monitor` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The global figures, and one row per enforcement point.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decisions` | object |  |  |
| `decisions.combined` | object |  |  |

## GET /admin-api/xacml/peps

`getXacmlPeps`

**The REMOTE Policy Enforcement Points that pull this repository, and whether they are deciding with the same policy this service holds**

Everything the Remote PEPs tab on /admin/xacml draws.

A REMOTE PEP runs in another process, holds its own copy of the engine and PULLS the enabled policies from GET /xacml/pep/policies. The pull is the contract; the nudge this service sends to `notifyUrl` when the repository changes is an optimisation over the polling interval and never a replacement for it, so a PEP that is never nudged still converges.

REGISTERING IS NOT A PERMISSION. An unregistered PEP can pull and enforce exactly as well — GET /xacml/pep/policies requires no credential, because a policy is a rule and a rule nobody can read is a rule nobody can check. What a row buys is this listing and an address for the nudge.

`current` is a COMPARISON this service performs between `syncToken` on the row and the repository's own, not a claim the PEP makes; `stale` is how long since it was last heard from against xacml.pepStaleAfterS and changes nothing this service does. The decision counts are the PEP's own, cumulative in its process — this service saw none of those decisions, which is what a remote PEP is — so a PEP that restarts makes them go down.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The register, and what each PEP last reported.

## GET /admin-api/xacml/policies

`getXacmlPolicies`

**The policy repository, with the type-check problems of each**

Everything the Policies tab on /admin/xacml draws.

THE STORE IS `ou=policies` IN THE EMBEDDED DIRECTORY — that container IS the repository rather than a copy of one, so an `ldapmodify` of `xacmlPolicyDocument` changes what the PDP decides on the next request.

EXACTLY ONE POLICY IS THE ROOT. A PDP evaluates one document and reaches the rest through PolicyIdReference, so the root is where evaluation starts; a repository with none decides nothing and reports `root: null`.

`templates` is what POST /admin-api/xacml/create-from-template will build, with the parameters each takes.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/xacml` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-expression-designator

`setXacmlDesignator`

**Make an expression an attribute reference**

An `<AttributeDesignator>`: reads an attribute out of the REQUEST, or out of the directory through the PIP when the id is a bare name or carries the `urn:sts:xacml:attribute:` prefix.

**IT RETURNS A BAG**, always, even when it finds exactly one value — which is why `string-one-and-only` exists and why most functions need it wrapped. Nothing in this engine ever holds a bare value, so there is no code path where somebody has to remember to wrap one.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-expression-selector

`setXacmlExpressionSelector`

**Replace an expression with an AttributeSelector**

An XPath over the `<Content>` of a request category, rather than a named attribute — and it returns a BAG exactly as a designator does, so most functions still need a `one-and-only` around it.

The namespace bindings its prefixes need TRAVEL WITH THE DOCUMENT: a prefix in the path means nothing without one, and an unresolvable prefix is an empty bag, which is NotApplicable, which looks exactly like a policy that decided you may not. Set them with edit-selector.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-expression-variable

`setXacmlVariable`

A `<VariableReference>` to a `<VariableDefinition>` in the same policy. The reference is checked at write time, so one naming a variable that is not there is refused rather than deciding Indeterminate.

## POST /admin-api/xacml/set-root

`setXacmlRootPolicy`

**Choose the policy the PDP starts from**

Clears the flag on the incumbent first, because the store refuses a second root. Done in that order deliberately: a failure then leaves the repository with NO root rather than with two, which is the recoverable one of the two bad states.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-policies, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-editor, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-peps, POST /admin/xacml/policies, POST /admin/xacml/editor and POST /admin/xacml/peps` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The policy's directory entry name. |
